newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arab police chiefs meet in Algiers on "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Arab police chiefs meet in Algiers on "terrorism".

text.p: Police and security chiefs from more than 20 Arab countries started on Monday a three-day conference in Algiers to chart a common strategy to fight "terrorism", the Algerian official news agency APS said.

Algerian Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour and other officials attended the opening session at Algiers' el Aurassi hotel, alongside Arab interior ministers' council secretary-general Mohamed Ben Ahmed Essalem, APS said.
Last year, Algerian security forces discovered and defused a car bomb in the hotel parking lot during a meeting of local officials.

The Arab security chiefs are to plan a strategy to counter "terrorists" - Algeria's official term for Moslem fundamentalist radicals blamed for violence in several Arab countries, including Gulf states, Algeria and Egypt.

Algeria, experiencing nearly five years of violence in which an estimated 50,000 people have died, said the police gathering was a signal of solidarity from other Arab governments with its government struggle against Moslem rebels.

"The Arab countries have decided to meet in Algiers to show solidarity with Algeria undergoing trials stemming from fanatical terrorism and fundamentalism," Algeria's national security chief colonel Ali Tounsi told APS.
